entries.description:
A type as a value — what TypeOf answers about a value and Type(name) answers by name, and what a type comparison is made against: `TypeOf(Value) = Type("Number")`. Two types are equal when they are the same class. String(type) is its registered name — "Number", "Table", "CatalogRef.Goods".

A TypeDescription is built from types — one, or an Array of them — and its Types() answers with them.

A Type is made by those two functions, not by New: `New Type(...)`, whatever it is given, makes a type that names no class, and the first use of it raises. A Type has no properties or methods of its own.
entries.parameters:
name — a registered type's name (Type).
value — any value (TypeOf).

entries.signature: New TypeDescription(types : string | Array | Type [, number : QualifierNumber [, date : QualifierDate [, string : QualifierString]]])
entries.description:
Which types a place holds — a column, a field, a parameter — and how each is limited: the digits of a number, the part of a date kept, the length of a string. A value table's column is declared with one (`Columns.AddColumn("Amount", New TypeDescription("Number"))`), and AdjustValue brings any value to it.

The types come first: a text of names separated by commas (`"Number, String"`, `"CatalogRef.Goods"`), an Array of Type values, or one Type. A name that is no type refuses the whole description ("Error initializing object 'TypeDescription'"). "Any" names nothing, and a description of nothing limits nothing.

The qualifiers follow, each in its fixed place — number, date, string — and one NOT GIVEN LIMITS NOTHING: a number unrounded, a date with its time, a string of any length. A place is skipped with an empty argument: `New TypeDescription("String", , , New QualifierString(50))`. A qualifier shapes its own kind only — a string's length means nothing to a number.

Without arguments the description is empty: it names no type, ValueIsFilled answers False, and AdjustValue hands any value back as it came. String(description) lists its types by name — "Number, String"; an empty one gives "".
entries.parameters:
types — a text of type names separated by commas, an Array of Type, or a Type.
number — a QualifierNumber; left out, a number is not limited.
date — a QualifierDate; left out, a date keeps its time.
string — a QualifierString; left out, a string has any length.

entries.description:
Whether the description names this type, among its own. The argument is a Type — Type("String") or TypeOf(value) — and anything else raises ("A value of type 'String' is not 'Type'"), so a type's name in quotes is not enough.

It compares the types the description LISTS, one by one; it does not ask what a listed family admits: a description of `"AnyRef"` does not name a catalog's reference type, though AdjustValue lets that reference through.

Brings a value to the description — the value a field of this type would hold if the value were written into it.

A value of a type the description names is kept, shaped by its qualifier: a number rounded to the scale (half away from zero — 2.5 becomes 3, -2.5 becomes -3) and cut to the most its digits hold, a date to its day or its time of day, a string cut to the length and, when fixed, padded with spaces.

A value of another kind, when the description names ONE type, is read as that type: "45.2" becomes 45.2 for a Number, "" becomes 0, 5 becomes "5" for a String, 1 becomes True for a Boolean. A text that is not a number raises rather than turning into 0. A value the type cannot be made from becomes the type's empty value; with several types named and the value of none of them, the answer is Undefined.

Without an argument it answers with the EMPTY value of the type — 0, "", the empty date, False, an empty reference — when the description names exactly one type, and Undefined otherwise. An empty description hands any value back unchanged.
entries.parameters: value — the value to bring to the description; left out, the type's empty value is made.
entries.return_descr: The adjusted value, or the type's empty value, or Undefined.
entries.example:
Desc = New TypeDescription("Number", New QualifierNumber(5, 2));
Message(Desc.AdjustValue("45.257"));    // 45.26
Message(Desc.AdjustValue(123456.789));  // 999.99 — the most five digits hold
Message(Desc.AdjustValue());            // 0

entries.description: The types the description names, as an Array of Type, in the order they were given. An empty description answers with an empty Array. The Array is a new one each call: changing it does not change the description.

entries.signature: New QualifierNumber(digits : number = 0, scale : number = 0, nonNegative : boolean = False)
entries.description:
How a number is limited — the digits in all, the digits after the point, and whether it may be below zero. Given to a TypeDescription in the number's place.

A number brought to it is rounded to `scale` digits after the point, half away from zero (2.5 becomes 3, -2.5 becomes -3), and kept within what its digits hold, either sign: QualifierNumber(5, 2) holds at most 999.99, and 123456.789 becomes 999.99. A non-negative qualifier turns a number below zero into 0.

0 digits is NO LIMIT — and then the number is not rounded either, whatever the scale says. The digits run from 0 to 38 and the scale from 0 to the digits; anything else is refused with a message naming the number. Without arguments the qualifier limits nothing. It has no properties: what it holds shows in what AdjustValue makes of a number.
entries.syntax_block:
Q = New QualifierNumber(15, 2);
Q = New QualifierNumber(10, 0, True);
entries.parameters:
digits — the digits in all, 0 to 38; 0 is no limit.
scale — the digits after the point, 0 to digits.
nonNegative — True: a number below zero becomes 0.

entries.description:
Which part of a date is kept — given to a TypeDescription in the date's place. DateFractions.Date keeps the day and drops the time (00:00:00); DateFractions.Time keeps the time of day on the empty date (01.01.0001 10:20:30); DateFractions.DateTime keeps both.

Without an argument, or with an empty one, the qualifier keeps both, which is what a description given no date qualifier does too. It has no properties.
entries.parameters: fractions — a member of DateFractions; left out, DateTime.
entries.example:
Day = New TypeDescription("Date", , New QualifierDate(DateFractions.Date));
Message(Day.AdjustValue(Date(2026, 3, 4, 10, 20, 30)));   // 04.03.2026 00:00:00

entries.signature: New QualifierString(length : number = 0, allowedLength : AllowedLength = Variable)
entries.description:
How long a string may be — given to a TypeDescription in the string's place. A longer string is cut to the length; with AllowedLength.Fixed a shorter one is padded with spaces up to it, as a fixed-width column keeps it.

0 is NO LIMIT, not "cut to nothing": a string of any length passes as it is. The length runs from 0 to 65535; anything else is refused with a message naming the number. Without arguments the qualifier limits nothing. It has no properties.
entries.syntax_block:
Q = New QualifierString(50);
Q = New QualifierString(5, AllowedLength.Fixed);
entries.parameters:
length — the most characters, 0 to 65535; 0 is no limit.
allowedLength — a member of AllowedLength; left out or empty, Variable.

entries.description: Which part of a date a QualifierDate keeps: the day, the time of day, or both. Written DateFractions.<Name>.
The day only: the time becomes 00:00:00.
The time of day only, on the empty date: 04.03.2026 10:20:30 becomes 01.01.0001 10:20:30.
The day and the time, as the date is. A QualifierDate made without an argument keeps this.
Whether a QualifierString's length is a ceiling or the exact length: a variable string is only cut to it, a fixed one is also padded with spaces up to it. Written AllowedLength.<Name>.
A ceiling: a longer string is cut to the length, a shorter one stays as it is. The default.
The exact length: a longer string is cut to it, a shorter one is padded with spaces up to it.

A globally unique identifier — 16 bytes, written as 36 characters, `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`, in lower-case hex.

`New Guid()` makes a NEW one, different from every other. `New Guid(text)` reads one from its text: 32 hex digits, either case, with the dashes where they stand or none at all; braces are not read. A text that is not a guid raises "New Guid: '<text>' is not a GUID", and a value that is not a text is refused ("Error initializing object 'Guid'").

The nil guid, all zeros, is a guid too — `New Guid("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")` is accepted — and it is the EMPTY one: ValueIsFilled answers False for it.

A guid equals its own text: `G = String(G)` is True, the other side being read as a guid's text. String(G) gives the 36 characters. A guid has no properties or methods.
entries.parameters: text — the guid's text; left out, a new guid is made.
